scenario.description: Lina, a neighborhood seamstress, must decide whether to accept an actor's barter proposal for making a stage costume, then record the exact garment, payment, schedule, competing offer, and required materials with input from the people gathered in her sewing room.

shared_context.S1: Lina has been asked to make a costume for a small neighborhood theater production.
shared_context.S2: Lina makes the final decision about whether to take the commission and what terms to agree.
shared_context.S3: Marco, Tess, and Hugo are all present in Lina's sewing room while the costume arrangement is being discussed.
shared_context.S4: Lina's normal closing procedure uses a written ledger to record the agreed terms, relevant alternatives, and production requirements for a commission.
shared_context.S5: As part of that procedure, Lina takes a round-robin report: Marco states his complete proposal, Tess states her complete cash alternative, and Hugo states the production requirements he received from the stage manager.
shared_context.S6: Lina does not finalize until each of those three reports has been stated aloud; she then reads the draft agreement aloud and asks the relevant person to confirm every term before entering it in the ledger.
shared_context.S7: The ledger uses exact entries for the accepted partner, garment, payment, fitting date and time, delivery date and time, comparison offer, fabric requirement, and trim width.
shared_context.S8: For dates and times, Lina copies the agreed wording in the ledger as 'June 3 at 18:00' and 'June 15 at 18:00', without changing the numbers or adding ordinal wording.

PF1.text: Marco's exact proposal is eight one-hour pottery lessons plus $60 in cash in exchange for an 18th-century black waistcoat, with a fitting on June 3 at 18:00 and delivery on June 15 at 18:00.

PF2.text: Tess is ready to pay Lina exactly $300 in cash for a different costume commission of similar sewing complexity, with no barter involved.

PF3.text: The theater's stage manager told Hugo that this waistcoat must use flame-resistant black wool-blend fabric and include a reflective trim strip exactly 50 millimeters wide; Hugo has not yet shared that requirement with Lina or Marco.

acceptance_conditions: The commission must be accepted from Marco.
The garment must be an 18th-century black waistcoat.
The settlement must provide eight one-hour pottery lessons and a $60 cash adjustment.
The fitting must be scheduled for June 3 at 18:00 and delivery for June 15 at 18:00.
The $300 competing cash offer must be recorded for comparison.
The waistcoat must use flame-resistant black wool-blend fabric.
The waistcoat must include reflective trim exactly 50 millimeters wide.
The settlement must record the accepted partner, payment, schedule, competing offer, and material specifications.

decisive_facts.why: Marco's exact proposal changes the settlement to Marco, an 18th-century black waistcoat, eight pottery lessons, a $60 adjustment, and the June 3 at 18:00 fitting and June 15 at 18:00 delivery.
Tess's exact $300 cash offer changes the comparison record from having no concrete alternative to recording a $300 competing commission.

The stage manager's requirement changes the materials from unspecified fabric and trim to flame-resistant black wool-blend fabric with exactly 50-millimeter reflective trim and requires Hugo's fact to be cited.
